content_voiceover: This table compares the clinical and laboratory features of several inherited platelet function disorders, and it is exactly the kind of table boards love to test with vignette style questions. Glanzmann thrombasthenia has a normal platelet count and normal size, but shows absent aggregation with all agonists except ristocetin, which is the classic distinguishing lab clue, it is autosomal recessive and involves ITGA2B or ITGB3. GPVI collagen receptor defect and P2Y12 ADP receptor defect are both autosomal recessive with normal counts and size but specific aggregation abnormalities to their respective agonists. Thromboxane A2 receptor defect is autosomal dominant. Then we get to the two storage pool diseases with associated syndromes, Chediak Higashi syndrome, which features albinism, eczema, recurrent infections, and lymphohistiocytosis, caused by LYST mutations, and Hermansky Pudlak syndrome, which features albinism plus pulmonary fibrosis and lysosomal storage disease, caused by several HPS genes. Scott syndrome has entirely normal aggregation testing because the defect is in membrane phospholipid scrambling, not aggregation. Finally, Bernard Soulier syndrome stands out because it is the only one here with a decreased platelet count and large platelets, showing absent aggregation specifically with ristocetin but normal response to other agonists, essentially the mirror image of Glanzmann.
keypoints: Glanzmann thrombasthenia: absent aggregation to all agonists except ristocetin
Bernard Soulier syndrome: absent aggregation only with ristocetin, large platelets, low count
Chediak Higashi syndrome pairs platelet dysfunction with albinism and recurrent infections
Hermansky Pudlak syndrome pairs platelet dysfunction with albinism and pulmonary fibrosis
Scott syndrome has normal aggregation because the defect is phospholipid scrambling
keypoint_voiceover: The single most testable contrast here is Glanzmann versus Bernard Soulier. Glanzmann loses aggregation to everything except ristocetin, while Bernard Soulier loses aggregation only to ristocetin and has large platelets with a low count. Also remember Chediak Higashi and Hermansky Pudlak as the two syndromic delta granule disorders with albinism.
